paper_name: 80_G.S. Frankel, R.C. Newman, C.V. Jahnes, M.A. Russak, J Electrochem Soc, 140 (1993) 2192-2197.pdf

alloy.preparation: Sputter-deposited thin film, thickness 1000-2000 angstrom. Washed with water; no other surface pretreatment. Masked with a sputter-deposited oxide film and pressed face upward against the bottom of a Plexiglas cell with a Viton O-ring. Aged 2-4 years in laboratory air in plastic boxes at room temperature (aged means more than one year after deposition).
alloy.microstructure: Pure Al film.

test_method.procedure_description: Scanned anodically from open circuit at 1 mV/s until a stable pit formed; scan stopped and potential held. Pit growth imaged. Subsequently potential stepped downward by 10-100 mV with 15-120 s holds (about 15-20 s near pitting, longer holds and 10 mV steps near repassivation). The downward sequence measures repassivation and is not itself a pitting threshold.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Stable pit formation evidenced by an abrupt and prolonged increase in current.

experiments.result_note: Figures 1-4, repeated pure-Al aged markers; visually digitized. Separate plotted outcomes; no error bar or mean is inferred.

The downward sequence measures repassivation and is not itself a pitting threshold.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Stable pit formation evidenced by an abrupt and prolonged increase in current.
